nodes.label: Linde (Product)
nodes.rationale: Success is defined as two people actually meeting, not as sign-ups, so every feature exists to move from 'I see someone nearby' to an agreed time.

nodes.label: Senior Users (65+)
nodes.rationale: Mostly not comfortable with technology: they distrust anything that looks like a form and give up when something is unclear, which drives one-action screens, worded buttons and large type.

nodes.label: Student Users (often international)
nodes.rationale: Comfortable with apps and need no hand-holding; they want everyday German practice with a real person and have weekday-afternoon time.

nodes.label: Two Roles, One App
nodes.rationale: `student` and `senior` chosen once in onboarding and never changeable; each role only sees the other. Both sides sign up for themselves - a profile IS an auth user, nobody administers anyone else's account.

nodes.label: Meine Karte (One Offer Per Person)
nodes.rationale: Exactly one offer per person with only two own fields (availability as free text, description); location comes from the profile. Deleting asks for confirmation.

nodes.label: Location is Postal Code Only
nodes.rationale: Location belongs to the person, not the offer (migration 0005), so somebody without an offer can still search; asked once in onboarding step 2 and pre-filled into both the offer form and the search filter. No street, no house number, no device coordinates; distances rounded to 'ca. 3 km'.

nodes.label: Always-Visible Discover Location Filter
nodes.rationale: Postal code plus 5/10/25/50/100 km radius with 25 km pre-selected, kept always visible rather than behind a sheet so seniors never have to discover a hidden control.

nodes.label: Connections (Request, Accept, Chat)
nodes.rationale: A request carries a written message, the recipient accepts or declines, and an accepted request becomes a chat with an unread badge.

nodes.label: Passwordless Login
nodes.rationale: Google, Apple or a 6-digit e-mail code; no phone number and no password, removing the single hardest step for non-technical users. Onboarding is three short steps: role, profile, interests.

nodes.label: Weekly Distinct Offer Views
nodes.rationale: Counted as distinct people per week, once per person per day, so refreshing a page cannot inflate the number shown as '34 Personen haben Ihr Angebot diese Woche angesehen'.

nodes.label: Age as a Chip, Stored as birth_year
nodes.rationale: Age is never shown next to a name - it is a fact among facts, not a headline - and is stored as `birth_year` rather than an age so it cannot go stale.

nodes.label: Not a Marketplace
nodes.rationale: No price, transaction, ratings, reviews, bookings or calendar. That restraint is the point: a rating system or booking flow would turn company into a service.

nodes.label: Post-and-Browse Classifieds Mechanic
nodes.rationale: Borrowed from eBay Kleinanzeigen - one offer per person, a radius location filter, scrollable cards - because that pattern is already familiar to German users of every age.

nodes.label: German Throughout, Formal Sie
nodes.rationale: Formal address matters specifically for the senior audience.

nodes.label: No Botanical Imagery
nodes.rationale: Despite the name Linde, no leaves, trees, plants or flowers: it would read as a flower shop or a wellness app. Iconography is plain geometry - circles, rings, pills.

nodes.label: Linde Brand System (Type and Palette)
nodes.rationale: Bitter for headings/names, Karla for body and buttons; ivory #F6F1E3, surfaces #FFFCF4, ink #2F2B1E, forest green #55713F for primary actions, gold #C99A3E for tags and badges only - never a primary button. Voice is plain, warm, respectful: short sentences, no jargon, no exclamation marks, no emoji.

nodes.label: Accessibility and Inclusion Commitments
nodes.rationale: Body text >=17px mobile / never <15px, tap targets >=44px and primary buttons >=60px, text contrast >=4.5:1 and control boundaries >=3:1 (muted grey and input borders were darkened for this), no icon-only controls, animation under 300ms respecting prefers-reduced-motion, platform autofill for the one-time code, and German screen-reader labels with gendered terms written out ('Seniorinnen und Senioren') because screen readers mispronounce the colon form.

nodes.label: One Clear Action Per Screen
nodes.rationale: A senior should never have to work out which of three buttons is the one that matters.

nodes.label: Nothing Hidden Behind an Icon or Menu
nodes.rationale: Buttons carry words and the location filter is always visible, never behind a sheet.

nodes.label: The Database Protects People, Not the Interface
nodes.rationale: Location stays at postal-code precision, names may be shortened, and messages are readable only by the two people in the conversation - enforced below the UI.

nodes.label: Reversible, and Confirmed Before Destructive
nodes.rationale: Delete asks first; a role, once chosen, is stated as permanent before it is picked.

nodes.label: The Meeting Happens Outside the App
nodes.rationale: No booking, calendar or reviews - the chat is where people agree and the app steps back. The first meeting happens in public (cafe, park, walk) and the chat says so.

nodes.label: Rare, Short Sessions
nodes.rationale: Nobody uses Linde every day, so nothing may rely on the user remembering how it worked last time.

nodes.label: UNESCO Projekttage School Project
nodes.rationale: Built in one week by a team of five; web ships on Vercel, mobile is tested through Expo Go and not published to any store. It ends in a presentation where the app must work on an unfamiliar device and network - which is why nothing may depend on an external service that can fail that day.

nodes.label: Seed Data is Local-Only Test Data
nodes.rationale: `supabase/seed.sql` holds five demo people and must never reach the live database, because its shared password is published in the README.

nodes.label: Placeholders, Not Invented Evidence
nodes.rationale: No real user photos (avatars are hatched placeholders with initials), no real support number ([IHRE SERVICENUMMER]), and no real users, testimonials or usage figures - the '34 Personen' view count is sample data.

nodes.label: Open: Radius Search Not Yet Functional
nodes.rationale: `profiles.lat`/`lng` are empty and no `postal_codes` table exists yet, so the filter cannot search by distance. This contradicts README's Distance search section, which describes `postal_codes` as a shipped migration.

nodes.label: Open: Affordability of Sign in with Apple
nodes.rationale: Needs an Apple Developer account at 99 EUR/year, including for the web version; Google and e-mail are free.

nodes.label: Open: Which City the Project is Set In
nodes.rationale: Seed data uses Osnabrueck, design mockups use Muenchen; they must agree before the presentation.

nodes.label: Claude Design Canvas UI Design
nodes.rationale: A complete UI design for both platforms: login, three onboarding steps, Discover, request, offer (empty/form/live), contacts, chat and the web equivalents.
